pass_a_gloss: Logos 3. [Lemma, Isaiah 3:12:] My people, your exactors glean you, and those who demand rule over you. Having explained beforehand most clearly and very plainly that the country of the Jews will be sick with desolation of every good, and having told what will happen to those who acted drunkenly outrageous toward Christ, he persuades again beforehand to keep away from the offences, and with the words from gentleness he all but enchants usefully, moving toward the better, and teaching to refuse those who had become causes of all evils to them. For I do not think one must love to be subject to those whose lot is to lead, even if they attempt to teach nothing of all the things leading to benefit, nor yet [...] to deem worthy of slander what would justly be believed to be set in the portion of baseness. For virtue of a teacher is to be able to carry those being tutored toward exact knowing of the profitable, and to show as counterfeit what by nature harms, and to order to refuse what is accustomed to wrong. And worthy of every praise would be also those counted among disciples, if they should look not simply at the reputations of those teaching, but at the nature of the things, and should marvel at those teaching, if some should be upright and knowing, and introducers of the best things, and should blame those whose aim may not be such. For some pasture the flocks of sheep in mountains and glens; but if a pit should lie beside the flocks, or a precipice of mountains, the sheep walk around, and do not let themselves down toward death; for they are tutored as through an inborn law toward the need to spare their own life. Then how is it not absurd if in the irrational animals this appears to prevail, but in us ourselves, although being rational, the knowledge of the useful and necessary toward life is not? It is needed therefore, even if some of those appointed into teachers and guides should choose to carry us away to the things not fitting, not simply to love to bear with it, nor yet to follow without examination toward what seems good to them, but to test each of the things to be done [...] to go toward what is most of the things accustomed to benefit. So the leaders of the Jews, that is, the scribes and the Pharisees, were clever toward the need to collect the gains of the moneys, and to gather the gift-bringings from the peoples, firstfruits, tithes, and as many things as the law to those whose lot was to be priests into lot [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Logos 3. “My people, your collectors glean you bare, and those who demand payment rule over you” (Isaiah 3:12).

Having declared beforehand, very plainly and quite clearly, that the land of the Jews would suffer the loss of every good thing, and having set out what will happen to those who behaved outrageously toward Christ, he again tries to persuade them in advance to keep away from their offences. With gentle words he all but charms them, to their profit, moving them toward what is better and teaching them to reject those who had become the cause of all their evils.

For I do not think one ought to be fond of submitting to those whose lot is to lead, if they attempt to teach nothing of what serves for profit; nor indeed … worthy of censure what may justly be believed to belong among wicked things. For the excellence of a teacher lies in being able to bring those in his charge to an exact knowledge of what is profitable, to expose as counterfeit whatever by nature does harm, and to bid them refuse what usually does wrong.

And those who are counted among disciples would deserve every praise if they looked not simply at the reputations of their teachers but at the nature of the matters themselves; if they admired their teachers, provided these are upright and knowledgeable and guides to what is best, and found fault with those whose aim is not of this kind.

Some men pasture flocks of sheep on mountains and in glens. But if a pit lies beside the flock, or a mountain precipice, the sheep walk around it and do not throw themselves down to their death; for they are taught, as by an inborn law, that they must spare their own life. Is it not absurd, then, that this should plainly prevail among irrational animals, while in us, though we are rational, there is no knowledge of what is useful and necessary for life?

So even if some of those appointed as our teachers and guides should choose to lead us toward what is not fitting, we must not simply be content to bear with it, nor follow without examination wherever they please; rather, we must test each thing that is to be done … to go toward whatever most often does good.

Now the leaders of the Jews, that is, the scribes and the Pharisees, were clever at collecting gains of money and gathering in the people’s offerings: first fruits, tithes, and all that the Law, as a portion for those whose lot was to serve as priests …

choices.why: καλαμάομαι, to glean after the reapers; the collectors take even what is left.

choices.english: he all but charms them, to their profit
choices.why: Gentle words that win them over, for their good.
κιβδηλεύω of false coin; the teacher shows harmful things for what they are.
Even sheep avoid a precipice by nature; rational people should do no less.
Disciples must test what their teachers bid them do.
